slides.heading: Line Through Points
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Line Through Points, a very hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Maximum number of the given (unique, integer) points lying on one straight line.
For each anchor, count normalised slopes (reduced by gcd, sign-canonicalised).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Maximum number of the given (unique, integer) points lying on one straight line. For each anchor, count normalised slopes (reduced by gcd, sign-canonicalised).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Fix an anchor point; points on the same line through it share a normalised slope.
slides.narration: Fix an anchor point; points on the same line through it share a normalised slope.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. For each anchor, map slopes to counts
2. Normalise slopes with gcd and sign
3. Track the largest count plus one
